bullets.title: SMCI blowout preannounce drives AI infrastructure rally; NVDA supply chain expanding aggressively
bullets.body: Supermicro raised F1Q revenue guidance to $18.5–19.5B vs prior $14.5–15.5B (27% raise, 280% y/y growth) with gross margins 12.0–12.5% vs prior 10.4–10.8% guidance, citing strong AI platform demand. NVDA announced multi-billion dollar capacity expansions with Amkor, IBIDEN, KYEC, SPIL, and others — substrate capacity up 2.5x over 3 years, testing capacity doubling from 2026 to 2027, SPIL optical engine capacity up 15x by mid-2027. Sympathy rally broad: DELL +6.8%, VRT +6.5% pre-market; S&P futures +0.24%.

bullets.title: SpaceX Q3 crushes across all segments; 2027 capex upgraded to $300B+, targeting $500B–1T ARR
bullets.body: SpaceX reported Q3 revenue of $14.6B (vs $12.8B est), 161% y/y, with Super Intelligence segment turning profitable for the first time at $7.6B revenue (+195% QoQ). Company guided Q1 2027 revenue $33–37B vs FactSet consensus $22.2B, and is targeting 10 GW incremental compute in 2027 reaching 12.5–13 GW total. UBS raised 2027 capex estimate from $124B to $310B; JPM raised PT to $500 from $240 on 20x 2028E GAAP EPS of $24.41.

bullets.title: SPCX-TSLA merger speculation: special committees formed, Musk confirms interest
bullets.body: SpaceX and Tesla boards formed special committees to explore a potential merger, with Elon Musk confirming interest on the earnings call. JPM noted regulatory considerations may be a factor; Hedgeye flags TSLA bullish if it holds $375 support but warns of historical -33% to -74% crash precedents in Quad4. TSLA changed from Bearish to Bullish trend on Hedgeye's Risk Range signals.

bullets.title: Hedge funds record net selling in Global Info Tech; AI net allocation at 38th percentile
bullets.body: Global Info Tech saw the largest 2-week % net selling on record (-3.3 standard deviations); net allocation to AI stocks is now at the 38th percentile. Global Fundamental L/S net leverage fell to near 3-year lows (4th percentile), with shorts outpacing longs ~5 to 1 and short leverage approaching the 99th percentile. Mag 7 net exposure rose to a new record high while US Semis/Software net exposure differential continues narrowing.

bullets.title: 10-year yield at 5.10%; Hedgeye warns of Quad4 risk, prefers XLV/RSP over QQQ
bullets.body: UST 10yr is back above 5.10% (trade signal), with Hedgeye's risk range at 5.06–5.33%. QQQ retail investors are down 14.6% in the past month; Hedgeye is selling QQQ bounces and prefers XLV, RSP, and hedged DJIA. SPX rated Bullish with range 7,616–7,850; Russell 2000 rated Bearish; NASDAQ Composite rated Neutral.

bullets.title: NFLX down ~6% pre-market: Q4 guide misses, ad revenue guidance cut to $2.7B from $3B
bullets.body: Netflix Q3 EPS $0.87 beat guidance of $0.82, revenue $12.87B in-line, but Q4 EPS guided at $0.67 vs consensus $0.73 and revenue $13.44B vs $13.52B consensus. FY26 ad revenue guidance cut to $2.7B from $3B on slower ad product rollout and partner integrations; FY26 revenue guided $51.1B (+13%) with 31.5% op margin. Morgan Stanley kept OW but cut PT to $77; Needham downgraded to Hold; 2027 revenue growth trajectory risks falling below 10% 'Rubicon.'

bullets.title: AT&T 3Q broadly beats; EPS guide raised to $2.40, long-term capex reduced; stock pressured by SpaceX wireless threat
bullets.body: AT&T reported Q3 revenue $32.32B vs $31.67B est, EBITDA $12.51B vs $12.32B est, EPS $0.65 vs $0.60 est; raised FY26 EPS guide to $2.40 from $2.25–2.35 and nudged EBITDA growth to upper 3–4% range. Fiber adds of 442K total beat, but postpaid phone adds of 379K missed ~408K consensus; fiber ARPU declined 4.3% y/y on promotional activity. Stock initial selloff attributed to SpaceX reaffirming plans to enter US wireless market in 2028, pressuring T, TMUS, and VZ.

bullets.title: META earnings tonight: buyside bar elevated; 2027 capex/opex guidance is the critical variable
bullets.body: META reports Q3 after close with stock up ~40% from lows on AI sentiment. JPM buyside focus is on 2027 opex ($210–225B vs Street ~$203B) and capex ($225–250B vs Street ~$200B), plus Muse engagement metrics and monetization timelines. Mizuho notes near-term earnings compression risk from AI investment and potential equity raise; speculation about equity issuance is circulating.

bullets.title: Data center construction boom accelerating: 83 GW under construction vs 44 GW in Jan 2026
bullets.body: GS Aterio data shows 83 GW of data center capacity currently under construction, up from 44 GW in January 2026, with ~30 GW potential activations expected in both 2027 and 2028. New announcements accelerated to 113 GW in Q3 2026 from 57 GW in Q2; average project size grew to 131 MW per building from 90 MW in Q3 2025. Third-party developers account for 60% of capacity under construction; behind-the-meter solutions expected to rise from 15% to 41% by 2027.

bullets.title: NVDA Rubin delay to Q2 2027 flagged by Hedgeye as key bear risk; neocloud financing stress building
bullets.body: Hedgeye removed its NVDA long, citing Rubin mass production delayed to Q2 2027 from buyside expectations of late Q4 2026/early Q1 2027 per 4 supply chain sources. Concerns center on neocloud financing stress suppressing AI system purchases; Coreweave is Hedgeye's #1 short on leverage/counterparty exposure. CoreWeave also raised $34B in equity and bonds yielding 15%, raising questions about neocloud capital structure sustainability.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex trajectory: GOOGL +60%, MSFT +63%, AMZN, META all raising 2027 estimates sharply
bullets.body: 2027E capex estimates for hyperscalers are reaching extreme levels: GOOGL $329B (+60% y/y), MSFT $237B (+63%), AMZN $319B, META $211B (+20%). Rising treasury yields partly driven by compute-related debt issuance are weighing on sentiment; credit tail-risk protection costs are nearing equity put levels. JPM maintains Tactically Bullish stance, noting AI/tech pullback has not been accompanied by earnings deterioration.

bullets.title: Google announces OpenAI models available in Cloud Marketplace; competitive cloud dynamics escalating
bullets.body: Google launched OpenAI models (GPT-Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna) in Google Cloud's model garden, allowing customers to draw down existing cloud commitments and swap models dynamically. This positions GCP as a multi-model marketplace and signals intensifying competition with Azure/OpenAI partnership — a potential share-gain catalyst for Google Cloud into Q3 earnings.

bullets.title: Rotation from crowded AI Memory/infrastructure into Software and Analog semis underway
bullets.body: UBS Tech note flags positioning rotation from Memory/AI infrastructure into Software and Analog semis, with ON +3.4% and NXPI +3.2% pre-market. Enterprise Hardware/Networking remains most crowded in AI (Arista +27, Keysight +25, HPE +25 long crowding scores). TXN reports tonight with CQ3 revenue/EPS expected at high end of guidance ($6.05B/$2.48); CQ4 guidance seen at $5.8–5.9B above Street ~$5.7B.

bullets.title: CRM acquires Braze for $47.50/share ($5.7B); strategic fit solid but organic growth concerns raised
bullets.body: Salesforce is acquiring Braze at 5x CY27 revenue / 31x FCF to strengthen its Marketing Cloud and AI capabilities (Data 360, Agentforce integration). Multiple brokers (UBS, DA Davidson) downgraded BRZE to Neutral post-deal; strategic rationale viewed as sound but questions arise about CRM's organic growth pace given acquisition cadence.

bullets.title: Oil up 1.7% to $99.88 on Iran war-driven shipping surge; Goldman expects elevated freight rates to persist
bullets.body: WTI crude rose 1.7% to $99.88 on bullish API inventory data and a sevenfold surge in oil shipping costs tied to the US-Iran conflict. WTI 2027 futures are up 22% since early August near all-time highs at $86/bbl. Morgan Stanley projects global fuel market tightness through mid-2027.

bullets.title: US fiscal deficit widening; M2 accelerating; yield curve well below nominal GDP — inflation risk building
bullets.body: PSC Macro flags sharp divergence from 1990s: the US is in deficit and worsening (vs Clinton-era surplus), M2 growth is accelerating (vs slowing in early 1990s), and the entire yield curve remains well below nominal GDP. Rising healthcare, defense, and interest outlays are driving outlays while receipts stay flat from OBBA/tariffs; this dynamic historically creates conditions for excess formation and inflation persistence.

bullets.title: Memory stocks down 42% from peak; bottom-up fundamentals solid but AI capex sustainability is the bear case
bullets.body: JPM notes global memory shares (SEC, SKH, MU) down 42% from September 2026 peaks as markets price in a potential 2027 down-cycle, with Q/Q memory price trends turning negative. However, bottom-up fundamentals remain solid: spot prices trending up, HBM ASP negotiation bias to upside, extended LTA order visibility. Key risk: AI capex slowing to <$1.5T in 2027 from funding constraints would be the catalyst for a full down-cycle; memory stocks historically fall 49% peak-to-trough.

bullets.title: Earnings week: TXN tonight; MSFT, GOOGL, NOW reporting next week — tech-heavy calendar
bullets.body: Key earnings upcoming: TXN and META tonight (Oct 21 after close); CMCSA and SPOT Thursday Oct 22; VZ Monday Oct 26; GLW and STX Tuesday Oct 27; GOOGL, MSFT, NOW, and ETSY Wednesday Oct 28. Implied moves for mega-cap earnings are near 10-year highs; NVDA's implied move is +/-83bps for its November 18 report.

bullets.title: LRCX expected to guide Dec quarter ~$9B, ~$450M above Street; semis momentum intact
bullets.body: UBS Tech expects Lam Research to guide December revenue ~$9.0B, roughly $450M above current Street estimates, with management potentially raising 2026 WFE guidance to high-$150B range. Upside scenarios price $18–23.50 EPS at $300B–$400B WFE. TSMC and ASML delivered healthy earnings pre-market, supporting the semis bid.

bullets.title: JPM constructive on IG credit; JULI year-end target 85bp (13bp tighter); consumer backdrop strong
bullets.body: JPM's High Grade credit team maintains constructive stance with JULI year-end target of 85bp (currently ~98bp), citing healthy flows, attractive yields, and earnings supportive of IG. Consumer remains in 'very good shape' with strong spending and credit metrics; companies successfully passing through energy/tariff costs. Key watch items: OATs (French political risk), CoreWeave spreads, and Treasury supply.
